solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Double-checked about volume and article fitted

indicators.note: about means around, so the first phrase is split to go round the rest

parts.note: to double-check something is to make sure of it
a tome is a large book, a volume
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone carefully checks a book and an item that were installed together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double-checked' looks like a description of the article; it is a two-word phrase that splits around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes that are made to measure are tailored to the wearer, so they are fitted.

clue.text: Cat chewing softly on leg is washing

indicators.note: a cat chewing something holds it in its mouth, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: mog is British slang for a cat
p, piano, is the musical mark for softly
pins is slang for legs

explanation.surface: A cat chews at its own leg while grooming itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The cat surrounds P followed by PIN: MO(P PIN)G. A mog or moggy is everyday British slang for a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mopping a floor is cleaning it with water, a form of washing.

clue.text: Outsiders from Christchurch avoid being bitten by relative's dog

indicators.note: what is bitten sits inside the jaws of the biter, so these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: a father is a relative; the possessive is for the surface

indicators.note: the outsiders of a word are its first and last letters only

parts.note: first and last letters of the New Zealand city
to shun is to avoid

explanation.surface: Some animal in Christchurch tries not to get nipped by a family member's dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Christchurch is a city in New Zealand; only its two end letters are used, and the father's name swallows them with the word for avoid.
explanation.definitionFit: The dachshund is a long-bodied, short-legged German breed of dog.

clue.text: People already indicated distinctive character cycling

indicators.note: cycling sends the letters round so the front one moves to the back

parts.note: the ethos of a group is its distinctive character

explanation.surface: Riders already pointed out have a special character when on their bikes.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the first letter E of ETHOS to the end gives THOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: As a pronoun, those refers back to persons already mentioned or pointed out.

clue.text: Low grass area raised with 1000 steps far above

parts.note: a cow lows, that is, moos

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means reading it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a lawn is an area of grass
K stands for a thousand

explanation.surface: A low grassy spot is lifted up by a thousand stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A moonwalk is the steps an astronaut takes on the Moon, high above the Earth.

clue.text: Funny muscles on tongue contracted

indicators.note: a contracted word is shortened, losing its final letter

parts.note: abs are the abdominal muscles
a tongue is a language, here Urdu

explanation.surface: A comic's facial muscles and tongue tighten up.
explanation.definitionFit: Absurd means ridiculous, laughable, which is one sense of funny.

clue.text: Unloved bears beginning to navigate plain

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so the first word holds the other inside it

parts.note: not adored, so unloved

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: first letter of navigate

explanation.surface: Unloved bears set out to find their way across a plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' reads as animals, but it is the verb carry. 'Plain' looks like open country; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Unadorned means without decoration, which is to say simple or plain.

clue.text: Opponents crossing border to overturn rulers

indicators.note: overturning a down entry turns it upside down, reading bottom to top
crossing means straddling, so the pair of letters goes either side of the other word

parts.note: South and East are opponents at the bridge table
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: Enemies cross a frontier intending to topple the leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: Emirs are Muslim rulers, princes or commanders in parts of the Middle East.

clue.text: 24 hours, short date for salad item

parts.note: Friday is a day of 24 hours, shortened to its abbreviation
to date someone is to see them

explanation.surface: A rushed day and a brief appointment allow time only for some lettuce.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' looks like a reference to another clue in the grid, but here it is just a number: 24 hours make a day.
explanation.definitionFit: Frisée is curly endive, a frilly leaf used in salads.

clue.text: Image reduced: musical instrument

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the punctuation mark's name loses its last letter

parts.note: pic is short for picture, an image
the punctuation mark in the clue is itself named: a colon

explanation.surface: A caption saying a picture has been shrunk, before naming an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon is not mere punctuation: it is part of the wordplay, read as its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The piccolo is a small flute pitched an octave above the ordinary one.

clue.text: Comparatively uncertain discussing Guevara alongside Starmer

indicators.note: discussing means talking about, so the names are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Che Guevara, the revolutionary
Keir Starmer, the British politician

explanation.surface: A politician sounds less sure when talking about Che Guevara next to Keir Starmer.
explanation.walkthrough: Said together, the first names Che and Keir sound like the comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakier is the comparative of shaky, meaning more unsteady or less certain.

clue.text: Drunk Aussie not a problem

indicators.note: someone drunk is jumbled and unsteady, so the letters are rearranged
not means without, so the letter A is dropped from the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Australian who has been drinking is no trouble at all.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a point of concern or difficulty, a synonym of problem.

clue.text: Resolved row — shares chargers

indicators.note: something resolved has been worked out and settled anew, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boardroom dispute over shares has been settled, and the fees charged.
explanation.definitionFit: A charger is a horse ridden into battle, which is what a warhorse is.

clue.text: Alcohol consumed by Doctor Finlay regularly with tetchy manner

indicators.note: what is consumed goes inside the consumer, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
rum is an alcoholic spirit

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, here every second letter

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of Finlay

explanation.surface: Doctor Finlay, a TV GP, is often grouchy after his regular drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Finlay is the hero of a long-running British TV series about a country doctor, which makes 'Doctor' feel part of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumpily means in a bad-tempered, irritable way, a tetchy manner.

clue.text: Knock over small bird, one on wall

indicators.note: over means turned upside down, so in a down entry the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a rap is a knock
the tit is a small songbird
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone topples a little bird perched on a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'on' is used twice over in effect: once as letters, while the clue reads it as perched on.
explanation.definitionFit: A partition is a dividing wall within a room or building.

clue.text: Exposed fence raged being put behind bars

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of covering, so each word loses its outside letters

parts.note: fence without its first and last letters
raged without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone raged at a fence when they were jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: To encage is to shut in a cage, to put behind bars.

clue.text: Moist area after upsetting perfume

indicators.note: upsetting overturns things, so the letters are knocked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A damp patch left once something has been spilt can still smell nice.
explanation.definitionFit: To perfume something is to give it a pleasant scent, to aromatise it.

clue.text: Drunk man from Genesis, Banks in manor-house with wine

parts.note: Ham is a son of Noah in the Book of Genesis

indicators.note: the banks of a river are its two edges, so only the outer letters count

parts.note: first and last letters of manor-house
red is a type of wine

explanation.surface: A member of the band Genesis gets drunk on wine in a country house.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Banks was the keyboard player in the rock band Genesis, which makes 'Banks' look like a name rather than a selection instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Hammered is slang for very drunk.

clue.text: New second home housing king

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: housing something means holding it within, so one letter is put inside

parts.note: a den is an animal's home
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A new second home has room for royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means up to date or recent, a synonym of new.

clue.text: Curry not all there and breads oddly missing

parts.note: not all there means mentally unbalanced, mad

indicators.note: with the odd-placed letters missing, only the even-placed ones remain

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of breads

explanation.surface: A curry that is incomplete, with the bread strangely absent.
explanation.definitionFit: A madras is a fairly hot Indian-style curry named after the city now called Chennai.

clue.text: African beast present leaving with run to the west

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the letter for the next word drops out

parts.note: an award is a present given in recognition
W is the abbreviation for with

indicators.note: in an across entry, heading west means reading right to left

parts.note: to run is to flow, as water does

explanation.surface: An African animal is present but departing, running west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a link word, but it is the abbreviation that leaves the gift; 'run' is a verb meaning flow.
explanation.definitionFit: The aardwolf is an insect-eating hyena of southern and eastern Africa.

clue.text: Supporting homes for birds after destroying top wildlife habitats

indicators.note: destroying the top of a down word removes its first letter

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
birds live in nests

explanation.surface: Backing nesting boxes after the destruction of the canopy where animals live.
explanation.definitionFit: Forests are large wooded areas that provide habitat for many animals.

clue.text: Party justifies tax squeezes

indicators.note: the phrase squeezes, holding within it, a run of letters spanning its words

parts.note: letters across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A political party defends tightening taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks political but means a festive gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a festival or celebration, a kind of party.

clue.text: Original theory radical backed with success is start of movement

indicators.note: backed means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: rad, short for radical
a win is a success
taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter alone

parts.note: first letter of movement

explanation.surface: A new radical idea, once supported and successful, launches a movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original' looks like it means new, but it points to Darwin's book On the Origin of Species.
explanation.definitionFit: Darwinism, evolution by natural selection, was set out in On the Origin of Species, making it the Origin theory.

clue.text: Many waterborne conveyances

definitions.meaning: second meaning: flat floating platforms used for carrying

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a fleet of boats; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft of things is a large number, and a raft is also a simple floating craft.

clue.text: Hiding somewhere in America, make fun of westbound former PM

indicators.note: something hiding sits concealed inside something else
in an across entry, going west means reading right to left

parts.note: to rib someone is to tease them
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A former prime minister holed up in an American city is mocked as he heads west.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair was UK Prime Minister from 1997 to 2007.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair is a former British prime minister.

clue.text: Excellent support for woman, very old

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment for a woman
v is the abbreviation for very
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Praise for a woman's backing, which is very longstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravo is a cry of approval meaning well done, used as an exclamation like excellent.

clue.text: American very loudly voices concerns

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud
to air an opinion is to voice it

explanation.surface: An American is noisily expressing worries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Voices' looks like a noun but is the verb, as is 'airs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Affairs are matters of business or interest, things that are one's concerns.

clue.text: Prepares payment

definitions.meaning: second meaning: British slang for cash in hand

explanation.walkthrough: Readies is British slang for ready money, banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Readies is both the verb for makes ready and a slang noun for cash used as payment.

clue.text: Dross novel's confused with an esteemed literary work

indicators.note: confused letters are muddled up, so they are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive S included
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trashy book is mixed up with a respected classic.
explanation.walkthrough: Sons and Lovers is D. H. Lawrence's 1913 novel; the clue's joke is that its own letters make 'dross novel's an'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sons and Lovers by D. H. Lawrence is a celebrated English novel, an esteemed literary work.
